name: Google Cloud Identity
abstract: Google's Identity-as-a-Service (IDaaS) and enterprise mobility management (EMM) solution that powers Google Workspace and Google Cloud. Provides centralized directory services, single sign-on (SSO) via SAML 2.0 and OIDC, multi-factor authentication with passkeys and FIDO security keys, automated user provisioning (SCIM), and Context-Aware Access.

pricing.freeTierLimit: Up to 50 user licenses included (additional free licenses on request)

sla.scope: Cloud Identity Premium and Google Workspace

features.description: Standard workforce authentication using corporate Google account email and password managed in the Google Admin console.
Consumer social sign-in (e.g. Facebook, GitHub) is not supported for Google Workspace and Cloud Identity corporate workforce accounts.
Passkey authentication for passwordless sign-in using biometric sensors, device screen locks, or FIDO2 hardware tokens.
Google Workspace accounts do not support email magic link sign-in for primary authentication.
On-device phone prompts ('Google prompt' or 'Tap Yes on your phone') allow users to sign in without entering their password.
Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) 2-Step Verification using Google Authenticator or compatible RFC 6238 authenticator apps.
FIDO U2F security key hardware tokens supported for 2-Step Verification.
FIDO2 / WebAuthn security keys and platform authenticators supported for phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication.
Email verification codes are not supported as a second factor in Google 2-Step Verification.
SMS text message and automated voice call verification codes for 2-Step Verification.
Set of 10 printable, single-use backup verification codes for account recovery when primary 2SV methods are unavailable.
Google prompt push notifications sent to Android devices or iOS devices via Google apps to approve sign-in attempts.
Risk-based login challenges triggered by suspicious activity, new locations, or unfamiliar devices; Context-Aware Access provides conditional access policies.
Automatic re-authentication challenges required for sensitive actions (e.g. security changes, password modifications) and configurable session duration limits.
Google OpenID Connect provider support for web, mobile, and server-side applications with public discovery and UserInfo endpoints.
Google acts as a SAML 2.0 Identity Provider (IdP) for thousands of pre-integrated SaaS applications and custom SAML applications.
Service accounts and OAuth 2.0 JWT bearer token assertions for server-to-server and automated system access.
Inbound Single Sign-On allowing users to sign in to Google Workspace and Cloud Identity using third-party OIDC identity providers.
Inbound SAML 2.0 Single Sign-On allowing Google Workspace and Cloud Identity to delegate authentication to an external SAML IdP.
Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS) synchronizes users and groups from Microsoft Active Directory or LDAP; Secure LDAP service provides cloud LDAP directory lookups.
Federated SSO and automated provisioning integration with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory).
Bulk user creation and updates using CSV file uploads in the Google Admin console.
Google Admin SDK Directory API supports uploading pre-hashed user passwords using MD5, SHA-1, and crypt formats (DES, MD5, SHA-256, SHA-512).
Download user list from the Google Admin console to Google Sheets, CSV, or JSON format.
Bulk user updates and deletions supported via CSV re-upload and Admin SDK Directory API batch operations.
Uploading a CSV file in the Admin console updates existing user profile information based on matching primary email addresses.
Inbound SCIM 2.0 provisioning API allows external Identity Providers (such as Microsoft Entra ID or Okta) to push real-time user lifecycle events into Google Workspace.
Automated outbound user provisioning automatically provisions and deprovisions accounts in supported SaaS applications from the Google Admin console.
Group synchronization and group membership updates via Inbound SCIM 2.0, with administrative lock-synced-groups capability.
Google Workspace does not support Just-In-Time (JIT) dynamic user provisioning during SSO sign-in; users must be pre-created via Directory API, CSV, GCDS, or SCIM.
End users can manage their security settings, 2SV methods, personal info, active sessions, and devices at myaccount.google.com.
Administrators can immediately suspend user accounts in the Admin console or via Directory API to prevent sign-in and revoke access tokens.
Custom user attributes schema allows storing custom fields in user profiles via the Admin console and Directory API.
Custom user schemas support up to 100 schemas per domain, 500 fields per schema, and up to 4 KB per field value.
Granular user search in Admin console and Directory API with query filters for email, name, organizational unit, and custom attributes.
Role-Based Access Control with prebuilt administrator roles (Super Admin, User Management, etc.) and granular custom administrator roles.
Hierarchical Organizational Units (OUs) for policy inheritance, combined with multi-domain support (secondary domains and domain aliases).
Admin enforcement of minimum and maximum password length, complexity requirements, password expiration, and prevention of password reuse.
Username guidelines enforcing allowed character sets, prefix/suffix limitations, domain association, and reserved system names.
Attribute-Based Access Control via Context-Aware Access evaluating device state, user identity, IP subnet, and geographic location.
Granular access level policies applied per application, organizational unit, and security group via Context-Aware Access.
OAuth 2.0 authorization scopes, Google Cloud IAM roles, and API client access controls configured in the Admin console.
Google Cloud and Google Workspace undergo independent annual SOC 2 Type II audits.
Certified compliant with ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, and 27018 standards.
Google provides a HIPAA Business Associate Amendment (BAA) for covered services.
Compliant with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) Level 1.
CSA STAR Level 2 Certification and Attestation for cloud security assurance.
Authorized at FedRAMP High and Moderate baselines for US government compliance.
Data Export tool for organization-wide customer data export and Google Takeout for user data portability.
Admin user deletion purges user profile data from Google systems in compliance with GDPR right to erasure.
OAuth consent screen configuration for internal and external app authorization requests in Google Cloud Console.
Data regions policy enables administrators to specify US, Europe, or Global storage locations for covered data.
Admin console audit and investigation logs retained for 6 months across user, admin, login, and token activities.
Continuous export of Google Workspace and Cloud Identity audit and report logs to Google Cloud BigQuery.
Security center providing a unified security dashboard, security health recommendations, and an investigation tool.
Data at rest is automatically encrypted by default using AES-256 encryption across all Google infrastructure.
All data in transit is encrypted using TLS 1.2+ between user devices, Google data centers, and external endpoints.
Client-side encryption (CSE) and Cloud External Key Manager (Cloud EKM) integration allowing customers to control encryption keys.
reCAPTCHA Enterprise and automated risk engines continuously detect and mitigate automated bot sign-in attempts.
Automated account lockout, login rate limiting, and suspicious sign-in verification challenges block brute-force attacks.
Google sign-in security analyzes IP reputation, geo-velocity, and abnormal sign-in velocity to throttle or challenge traffic.
Password Checkup technology warns users and administrators when compromised or publicly breached credentials are used.
Google Credential Provider for Windows (GCPW) secures Windows device logons using Google account credentials and 2SV.
Context-Aware Access rules and domain-specific access policies restrict resource access to authorized organizational contexts.
Google sign-in risk engine evaluates device signals, browser environment, operating system, and historical user sign-in behavior.
Custom corporate logo upload in the Google Admin console displayed across Google Workspace services and sign-in pages.
2-Step Verification enforcement, grace periods, and allowed verification methods configured independently per Organizational Unit or Group.
Centrally hosted, secure Google sign-in interface at accounts.google.com handling authentication, MFA, and recovery.
Google disallows OAuth authentication in embedded webviews (UIWebView/WebView) for security compliance with RFC 8252.
Custom company logos can be displayed on Google services, but login endpoints and root branding remain Google-hosted at accounts.google.com.
Sign-in interface and Google Admin console localized into more than 70 languages.
Google Identity Services (GIS) provides prebuilt 'Sign in with Google' and One Tap web and mobile UI components.
Comprehensive login audit logs, security charts, 2SV adoption tracking, and suspicious login reports in the Admin console.
Official Google APIs Client Libraries available for Node.js, Python, Java, Go, C# (.NET), and PHP.
Google Admin SDK (Directory API, Reports API) and Cloud Identity API for automated user, group, and device administration.
Published quotas and rate limits for Google Admin SDK Directory API, Reports API, and OAuth token endpoints.
Google Apps Script and Cloud Functions provide event-driven triggers and extensibility for identity and directory events.
The Google clasp command-line tool enables writing Google Apps Script automations in TypeScript with automated transpilation.
Custom URL mapping for Google Workspace service endpoints (e.g., mail.yourcompany.com, drive.yourcompany.com).
Google Cloud SDK (gcloud CLI) and open-source Google Apps Manager (GAM) command-line tools for directory and identity administration.
Official HashiCorp Terraform Google Provider supports provisioning and managing Cloud Identity groups, memberships, and policies.
Push notifications via webhook endpoints and Google Cloud Pub/Sub for Admin SDK Directory resource changes.
Company logo customization supported; full HTML/CSS modification of accounts.google.com is disallowed for security reasons.
Gmail routing rules, custom outbound SMTP relays, and dual-delivery gateways for integration with third-party email systems.
Custom user schema attributes can be mapped into SAML assertions, while OIDC tokens include standard Google OpenID profile claims.
Google AppSheet provides a no-code workflow and automation builder integrated with Google Workspace and Cloud Identity directory.
Google Cloud Billing API and Google Workspace Admin Billing for programmatic subscription and invoice management.
Workforce Identity Federation and service account impersonation provide secure identity and token exchange for AI agents and workloads.
Google deployed hybrid post-quantum key exchange (X25519Kyber768 / ML-KEM) in Google Chrome and across Google frontends.
Google published an official post-quantum cryptography transition roadmap detailing algorithmic migration phases across infrastructure.
OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with OpenID Connect for user authentication.
OAuth 2.0 refresh token grant for obtaining new access tokens without user interaction.
OAuth 2.0 implicit grant flow is supported for legacy applications but deprecated in favor of Authorization Code with PKCE.
OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628) for limited-input devices such as smart TVs, game consoles, and CLI tools.
OAuth 2.0 JWT Bearer Token Grant (RFC 7523) for server-to-server authorization using Google service accounts.
SAML 2.0 Profile for OAuth 2.0 Client Authentication and Authorization Grants (RFC 7522).
Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE - RFC 7636) supported with S256 and plain code challenge methods.
OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoint at https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth.
OAuth 2.0 token endpoint at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token.
OpenID Connect UserInfo endpoint at https://openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo.
OAuth 2.0 token revocation endpoint at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke.
Token validation endpoint at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/tokeninfo.
Device code authorization endpoint at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/device/code.
OpenID Connect discovery document published at https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration.
Authorization server metadata published at https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration.
OIDC prompt=none supported for silent authentication checks.
OIDC prompt=login forces the user to re-authenticate.
OIDC prompt=consent forces the authorization consent screen to be displayed.
OIDC prompt=select_account presents the account chooser interface to the user.
Client authentication via HTTP Basic Authorization header at the token endpoint.
Client authentication via client_id and client_secret in the request body at the token endpoint.
Service accounts authenticate using RSA private keys to sign JWT assertions sent to the token endpoint.
